en: Oṃ, O subtle one, twice; O peaceful one, twice; O self-controlled one, twice; O you who are without superimposition, without support, without agitation, and in nirvāṇa; O Yaśovatī of great splendor, empowered by the empowerment of all Buddhas, svāhā! With this Vairocana-dhāraṇī mantra, the raising of the staff at a caitya or similar site is performed.

oṃ sukṣme sukṣme śānte śānte dānte dānte āpamarope nirālambhe | nirākule | nirvāṇe | yaśovati | mahātejase sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī of Vairocana; with this mantra, one should insert the central axis (yaṣṭi) into stūpas and other such structures.
The *vyāyāma* (the distance between the two doorposts) is one-eighth of the temple's width;
it is adorned with foliage and its height is twice that measurement, which is recommended.

The width of the excellent palaces, consisting of eight or ten parts, is the central portion of the door; by that measure, the foliage [of the arch] is shown, and its double is the height of the door.
The *niryūha*, *bāhu*, *dehali*, and *āsā* are prescribed as being one-fifth of that.
Their joints and connections are well-knit, and their form and configuration consist of jewels and lotuses.

The arches, the shoulders, and the seventy-four [ornaments] are explained as its five parts. It is perfectly arranged with interconnected joints, and it stands correctly formed with the various patterns of jewels and lotuses.
Established upon the pure samādhis and so forth, it arises from the syllable HŪṂ as a great gateway;
through the purification of the faculties such as faith, it is endowed with excellent archways of meditative concentration.

Abiding in meditation free from defilement, that which is perfectly generated from the syllable *hūṃ* is the "Great Arch" (*mahānāsa*), consisting of the faculty of faith and so forth; and pure meditation is endowed with beautiful archways.
The practitioner should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over each of the gates;
in the eastern direction, he should establish the station with the Yamadviṭ mantra as before.

The mantra practitioner should perform the recitation one hundred and eight times for each of the gates as before; those stationed in the eastern direction and so forth [should be invoked] with the mantra of Yamāntaka,
and those situated in the southern direction with the mantra of the heroic king Prajñāntaka.
The location in the western quarter is [consecrated] with the heart-mantra of Padmāntaka.
One should properly worship the southern direction with the mantra of the heroic king Prajñāntaka; the western quarter with the heart-mantra of Padmāntaka;
and the location in the northern direction with the mantra of the heroic king Vighnāntaka.
One should well worship the well-proportioned, elevated, and upright gates according to the ritual procedure.

Those residing in the northern direction [are to be invoked] with the mantra of the heroic king Vighnantaka. The doors, which have been raised to their proper dimensions and well-delineated, should be properly worshipped according to the ritual.
This is the procedure for raising the doors (*dvārotthāpanavidhi*).
Thus concludes the ritual for raising the door-panels.
Situated upon jeweled slabs, endowed with perfect circumference and height,
rich in qualities such as being quadrangular, firm in substance, and possessing faultless proportions.

It rests upon a vajra adorned with jewels; it is perfectly endowed with circular and vertical proportions, possesses many qualities such as being square, and has a firm, unswerving, and well-situated core.
The pillars are composed of all the [auspicious] signs; they are situated upon pedestals consisting of the lion and other [emblems], representing the meditative absorptions (samādhi).
Through the purification of the liberation of emptiness (śūnyatā-vimokṣa), the vajras arise from the syllable HŪṂ.

Upon a lion throne and other such pedestals, which are perfectly situated within the samādhis of "All Pillars Equal at the Pinnacle" and so forth, there is a vajra born from the syllable *hūṃ*, purified by the liberation of emptiness.

Well-established in the cardinal and intermediate directions, one should recite for each direction the heart-mantras of the wrathful kings of those respective directions one hundred and eight times, in due order.

One should properly arrange [the deities] in the cardinal and intermediate directions; then, for each respective direction, the heart-mantra of the Wrathful King should be correctly recited one hundred and eight times, each in its proper sequence.
The ritual procedure for the raising of the pillar.
Thus concludes the ritual for fashioning the pillar.
It is appropriate to quickly state that for timber used in the construction of monasteries and similar structures,
the time when the leaves have not yet withered— such as during the asterism of Mṛgaśiras— is auspicious.
Upon a golden star-lotus, conjoined with the Kurukullā-dhāraṇī.

One who possesses speed should firmly grasp the timber while residing above the temple and other structures; at a time when the leaves are not yet withered, the asterisms such as Mṛgaśiras are praised. Upon a lotus made of gold and silver, one should place the form of Vidyāmātṛ in its proper position.

Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Homage to the eight great noble persons! Homage to the seven hundred million Buddhas! It is as follows: Oṃ hrīḥ hrīḥ hrīḥ! [To all] the nāgas of the Ananta family, the Vāsuki family, the Takṣaka family, the Śaṅkhapāla family, the Karkoṭaka family, the Padma family, the Mahāpadma family, the Balāhaka family, the Puṇḍarīka family, the Ghana family, the Megha family, and the Jaladhara family.

Of the Jīmūta lineage, the Saṃvarta lineage, the Airāvata lineage, the Kumuda lineage, the Kahmāra lineage, and the Saugandhi lineage—with the *phaṇaphaṇa* arrow, bind, bind! With the bow, strike, strike! With the blue lotus, grant fearlessness to those who are afraid! Like a cloud at the time of universal dissolution, cause them to descend; let the raining Nāgas be brought under control! *phuḥ kuru 2 phuḥ kārāpaya 2 phuḥ phuḥ oṃ kurukulle hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!*

Homage to the Jewel Tārā! Homage to the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas! Homage to the Noble Assembly of the Eight Great Nāgas! Homage to the Seven Classes of Nāgas! Thus it is said: Oṃ hrīḥ hrīḥ hrīḥ! To all the Nāgas: of the Ananta family, of the Vasuki family, of the Takṣaka family, of the Śaṅkhapāla family, of the Śaṅkhapāla family, and of the Karkoṭaka family.

Padmakuḷānām | Mahāpadmakuḷānām | Balahākuḷānām | Puṇḍarīkakuḷānām | Ghanakuḷānām | Meghakuḷānām | Jaladhārakuḷānām | Jīmūtakuḷānām | Saṃvartakuḷānām | Airāvakakuḷānām | Kumudakuḷānām | Kahlārahakuḷānām | Sugandhikakuḷānām | Hanahaneśvareṇa ||

Bind! Bind! Ts’a pe na! H’a tā ya tā tā ya! Au pa le na! Bhi tā nām! Ā pā yam! De hi pra lā ya! K’ā lai ba dzā la dhā ram! Ā be tā rā ya! Barṣa nā nā gā na ba śi ku ru ku ru phaṭ! K’ā rā pā ya k’ā rā pā ya phuḥ phuḥ! Oṃ kuru kulle hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! [This is] a very firm canopy, with many clusters [of ornaments] in the mandala, [measuring] the width of the altar and three times its height, a great canopy hanging down.
The maṇḍala is strewn with many collections of canopies adorned with extremely firm bird feathers; the great birds, possessing the proper proportions, hang down at twice the height of the pedestals.
Having recited the mantra of the glorious Uṣṇīṣacakravartin one hundred and eight times,
and having performed worship according to the ritual for offerings and fire-sacrifices, the one of great intelligence—
One should adorn [the image] consecrated with the water from the jar with an umbrella, garments, and sprouts.

Furthermore, for one hundred and eight times, one should perform the perfect recitation of the mantra of the glorious Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin, along with offerings, *bali* rites, and extensive procedures for fire oblations (*homa*). One should then confer the empowerment with water from the ritual vase and adorn [the deity] with parasols, garments, and petals.

Thus is the mantra: *Namaḥ samantabuddhebhyaḥ | Oṃ pratyaṅgiroṣṇīṣacakravarti, bind all yantras and mantras! Bind the realm of Indra! Bind the great realm! Bind the great rain! Bind the deity of the tree! Hold fast! Cut, cut! Split, split! Ciri, ciri! Śiri, śiri! Miri, miri! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! [Whatever fear or such has been created by anyone dwelling here, destroy it! Thus is the mantra. *Namaḥ samantabuddhebhyaḥ | Oṃ pratyaṅgiroṣṇīṣacakravarti, bind all yantras and mantras! Bind the realm of Indra! Bind the great realm! Bind the great rain! Bind the deity of the tree! Hold fast! Whatever fear or such has been created by anyone dwelling here, cut it twice, split it twice! Ciri, ciri! Śiri, śiri! Miri, miri! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!*

The mantra beginning with "kṛdbhayādikaṃ" is as follows: Namaḥ samantabuddhebhyaḥ oṃ prahyāṅgira uṣṇīṣacakravarti sarvayantrabandha | aindrabhubanaṃ bandha | mahābhubanaṃ bandha | mahāvr̥ṣṭibandha | vr̥kṣadevatāṃ bandha | rāya ai hā bāsīnāṃ yenakena cit kṛtabhayādikaṃ | chinda chinda | bindha bindhya | ciri ciri |
Gi ri gi ri | mi ri mi ri hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | This is the ritual for raising up those suffering from head diseases in monasteries and other such places.
This is the ritual for erecting wooden beams upon temples and other such structures.
